content: Eisenhower College was a small liberal arts institution named after U.S. President Dwight D. Eisenhower. It was located in Seneca Falls, New York, and began its operations with its inaugural class in 1968. The college's curriculum included mandatory courses that explored the history of civilization, spanning from the emergence of humanity to modern times. These courses covered a wide range of disciplines, including music, art, history, science, philosophy, and literature. Additionally, students were required to take courses in foreign languages and physical education. The campus was notable for its weekly, well-attended classes on modern music and human sexuality, which were held in a building known as the Red Barn. Another unique tradition at Eisenhower College was the annual Communication Arts Festival, which took place every April. In the absence of a fall homecoming tradition, this festival, often referred to as Comm-Arts weekend, provided an opportunity for students, alumni, and friends to reconnect and celebrate together. The event was characterized by the rainy spring weather typical of the Seneca Falls area. Eisenhower College graduated its final class in 1983. The institution had been acquired by the Rochester Institute of Technology in 1979, and the property was subsequently sold to the New York Chiropractic College, which continues to operate on the campus. As of 2006, an archive of materials related to Eisenhower College, donated by former professors and alumni, is preserved on the campus.
